skill.name: defi-protocol-templates
skill.description: Create DeFi protocol starting points for staking, AMMs, governance, lending, and flash loans. Use the templates as audited design inputs, not deployment-ready contracts.
skill.summary: Generate DeFi smart contract templates and review guidance for common protocol patterns.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The static script and command findings are false positives caused by Solidity require statements and Markdown code fences. No prompt injection, data exfiltration, or host command execution was found. Manual review found a high-risk content issue because simplified DeFi examples are presented as production-ready templates.

remediation.issue: Production-ready wording conflicts with simplified examples.
remediation.suggestion: Label the contracts as educational starting points or replace them with audited, version-pinned templates.

remediation.issue: AMM template lacks user safety controls.
remediation.suggestion: Add minimum output parameters, deadline checks, SafeERC20 transfers, reentrancy protection, and invariant tests before publishing.

remediation.issue: Flash loan repayment example is incomplete.
remediation.suggestion: After receiver approval, pull repayment with transferFrom or require direct repayment and document receiver contract requirements.
Implement proposal targets, calldata, timelock execution, quorum, and access controls before calling it a governance template.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe Production DeFi Template Claims
semantic_findings.description: The skill presents simplified Solidity examples as production-ready templates. The AMM, governance, and flash loan examples omit deployment-grade safety controls, which could lead users to copy unsafe fund-handling logic.

The evidence is direct, although some code may be intended as illustrative documentation.

content.value_statement: DeFi teams need starting points for common protocol patterns, but blank contracts slow design work. This skill provides Solidity templates and review prompts for staking, AMMs, governance, lending, and flash loans.
actual_capabilities: Drafts staking reward contract structures with accounting hooks and reward claim flows.
Shows a simple constant-product AMM with liquidity, swap, mint, and burn flows.
Outlines governance token and voting proposal mechanics.
Provides flash loan provider and receiver patterns for discussion.
Lists DeFi implementation resources and security best practices.
limitations: Templates require contract-specific testing, threat modeling, and professional audit before mainnet use.
Examples may need updates for current Solidity and OpenZeppelin versions.
The skill does not validate economic parameters, token behavior, or oracle design.
It does not replace legal, compliance, or protocol risk review.

use_cases.title: Prototype Protocol Logic
use_cases.description: Prototype staking, AMM, or governance flows before writing production contracts.

use_cases.title: Prepare Security Reviews
use_cases.description: Compare planned protocol logic against common DeFi controls and missing checks.

use_cases.title: Scope Web3 Features
use_cases.description: Translate DeFi feature ideas into implementation scopes for engineering discussion.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Staking Outline
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline a staking rewards contract for [token] with [reward model]. Include assumptions and safety checks.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt an AMM Template
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to adapt the AMM template for [token pair]. Explain fees, slippage controls, and test cases.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Governance Contracts
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design governance token and proposal flow for [protocol]. Include quorum, timelock, roles, and upgrade controls.

prompt_templates.title: Threat Model a DeFi Protocol
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review [protocol design] across staking, liquidity, governance, lending, and flash loan risks. Produce prioritized remediation.

output_examples.input: Draft a staking protocol for a liquidity mining campaign.
output_examples.output: A structured plan covering token roles, reward accounting, user flows, events, test cases, and audit checkpoints.

output_examples.input: Review an AMM design for launch readiness.
output_examples.output: A readiness checklist covering slippage controls, fee math, safe token transfers, reentrancy, oracle assumptions, and invariant tests.
A risk summary describing callback trust, repayment enforcement, liquidity checks, receiver validation, and monitoring needs.

best_practices: Treat every template as a starting point until tests and audits pass.
Pin compiler and library versions before adapting contract examples.
Add unit, integration, fuzz, and invariant tests for each protocol path.
anti_patterns: Deploy copied examples without adapting controls to the token and chain.
Ignore slippage, oracle, access control, and upgrade risks.
Assume flash loans are safe because repayment is checked once.

faq.question: Can this skill generate deploy-ready contracts?
faq.answer: No. It creates starting points that require testing, review, and audit before handling funds.

faq.question: Which protocols are covered?
faq.answer: It covers staking, AMMs, governance tokens, lending concepts, yield farming, and flash loan patterns.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it replace a smart contract audit?
faq.answer: No. Use it for design and implementation support, then get expert review before deployment.

faq.question: What inputs improve results?
faq.answer: Provide target chain, token standards, reward model, governance rules, and risk constraints.

faq.question: How should I use the output?
faq.answer: Use it to plan architecture, ask review questions, and guide implementation under expert supervision.
